title: Mean Streets
tagline: Little Italy. Big round at the bar.
about: A small-time hood in Little Italy tries to keep his reckless friend Johnny Boy out of trouble.
cue: Hit play on the jukebox and pour a round when Johnny Boy walks into Tony's bar.
faces: THE RED LIGHT’S ON. WE’RE OPEN.
Feast week. Everybody’s here. Nobody’s paying.
Charred onion and red pepper, hot mustard.
Fried dough, shaken hot in icing sugar.
Squid rings, crisp semolina coat, lemon.
Garlic, hot chilli, tomato, parsley, pecorino.
Chilled red over sliced white peaches. Jug 3.50.

    StartersSausage & peppersCharred onion and red pepper, hot mustard.Brought in from the feast stands.How to make it500g Italian sausages1 red capsicum, in chunks1 onion, in chunks50g hot mustard1 tbsp olive oilGrill the sausages over high heat, turning, until blistered and cooked through.Toss the capsicum and onion in oil and grill until charred at the edges.Slice the sausages thick and thread onto toothpicks with the capsicum and onion.Serve with the hot mustard.Fried calamariSquid rings, crisp semolina coat, lemon.Johnny Boy had two. Ask Tony.How to make it500g squid tubes250ml buttermilk100g fine semolina100g plain flour1 tsp salt500ml neutral oil, for frying2 lemons, cut in wedgesSlice the squid into rings and soak in the buttermilk for 30 minutes.Mix the semolina, flour and plenty of salt.Drain the squid and toss in the flour mix.Fry in 190°C oil in batches for 90 seconds each until pale gold.Salt and serve with lemon wedges.MainsPenne arrabbiataGarlic, hot chilli, tomato, parsley, pecorino.As hot as Johnny Boy's temper.How to make it4 garlic cloves, sliced1 tsp dried chilli flakes4 tbsp olive oil800g crushed tomatoes500g penne2 tbsp chopped parsley50g pecorino, gratedsalt, to tasteGently fry the garlic and chilli in the olive oil.Add the tomatoes, season well and simmer.Cook the penne until al dente and toss through the sauce with a splash of pasta water and parsley.Finish with the pecorino.SweetsZeppole in the bagFried dough, shaken hot in icing sugar.Eat them hot, feast week only.How to make it250g plain flour7g dried yeast1 tbsp caster sugar1 pinch salt200ml warm water500ml neutral oil, for frying60g icing sugarMix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and warm water into a sticky batter.Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.Drop teaspoons into 175°C oil and fry in batches for 3 minutes until puffed and golden.Drain, tip into a paper bag with icing sugar, shake and eat hot.DrinksFeast wine & peachesChilled red over sliced white peaches. Jug 3.50.Another round. Cash only.How to make it3 ripe white peaches1 tbsp caster sugar750ml light Italian red, such as Lambrusco secco or young ChiantiHalve, stone and thinly slice the peaches into a large jug. Sprinkle with the sugar and leave for 10 minutes.Pour over the light Italian red and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.Serve in tumblers with a spoonful of peach in each. Eat the peaches last.
